the development and testing of noninvasive EEG-based brain-computing interfaces for control of assistive devices.

we developed a noninvasive BCB system that can be implemented on a robotic manipulator and tested it on healthy subjects.

we have developed a novel EEG BCI system and signal processing algorithm for a 3-6-state communication paradigm, implemented a virtual robotic prosthetic system and successfully tested it with healthy participants.
we have developed an EEG BCI system that allows a paralyzed person to control a robotic arm using his or her brain activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high-performance BCI system can be built with a relatively small number of electrodes, and that a 3-state BCI system can have a high accuracy.
the performance of the EEG BCI system is highly individualized and is strongly dependent on the subject9s mental state and the quality of the EEG data collected.

EEG-based BBI may provide a viable alternative to invasive BCIs, especially when invasive BCI is not a viable option due to the nature of the injury or other medical conditions of the user, or when invasive BCI cannot be used at all due to ethical reasons.
